outline.chapter_title: FlashAttention-3: Accelerating Attention with Asynchrony and Low-Precision
outline.description: The Transformer architecture has become the foundational backbone of modern artificial intelligence, particularly in large language models (LLMs), where the attention mechanism serves as the primary computational bottleneck. Attention scales quadratically with sequence length ($N$), making it prohibitively expensive for tasks involving long contexts, such as reasoning over multiple documents, parsing large codebases, or analyzing high-resolution audio and video. As applications move toward handling these longer sequences to capture comprehensive information or maintain user history, the demand for faster and more efficient attention implementations becomes critical. outline.chapter_title: Foundations: Hardware Architecture and Execution Models
outline.description: The transformative power of \textsc{FlashAttention-3} rests not merely on algorithmic refinements but on a deep and granular understanding of the physical execution model of modern GPUs, specifically the NVIDIA Hopper architecture. To appreciate how over 750 TFLOPs/s are extracted from silicon in practice, one must look beyond abstract mathematical formulations and examine the tangible interplay between memory bandwidth, computational throughput, and the asynchronous nature of hardware resources. This chapter serves as a primer on the architectural foundations that \textsc{FlashAttention-3} explicitly leverages. outline.description: The acceleration of neural network training and inference on GPUs has historically been governed by the tension between massive computational throughput provided by Tensor Cores and the latency inherent in moving data from high-capacity global memory (HBM) to the restricted registers and shared memory of compute units. outline.chapter_title: FlashAttention-3:Breaking Sequential Dependencies via Intra-Warpgroup Overlapping Pipelining
outline.description: The theoretical limit of GPU performance in attention mechanisms is often dictated not by the raw parallelism of the hardware, but by the architectural dependencies inherent in the algorithmic design of previous generations. While \textsc{FlashAttention} and its successor, \textsc{FlashAttention-2}, successfully mitigated memory-bound bottlenecks through global optimization, they adhered to a rigid, step-wise execution model. This "synchronous" approach processes one sequence block entirely before moving to the next, forcing a strict sequential dependency between matrix multiplication (GEMM) and softmax operations.
